audience: a parent or patient-group leader without medical training

sentences.text: Constellate computed that Krabbe disease and Pelizaeus-Merzbacher spectrum disorder have somewhat similar symptom profiles, with a similarity score of 0.222 over 16 shared symptom terms, ranked 6 of 28 [e_00a92bfb7837].
This is an "inferred" link, meaning Constellate calculated it from overlapping symptom terms, and it is not a database finding [e_00a92bfb7837].
The top shared symptom is progressive spasticity [e_00a92bfb7837].
The causes recorded in curated databases differ: Krabbe disease is tied to the gene GALC, while Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease is tied to the gene PLP1 [e_3dbc42738b5a] [e_1dafbc162208].
Krabbe disease also has an inferred link to the gene PSAP, rolled up from the infantile form at confidence 0.475, and it may not hold for every form [e_2c5236d2f740].

Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease has two recruiting studies on ClinicalTrials.gov, one testing a drug called ION356 for safety and one tracking biomarkers and disease progression [e_ac2aac17eb1d] [e_1ea565934c51].
A research grant recorded in NIH RePORTER also targets this disease [e_e9a5dff2e63c].

These edges do not show that the Pelizaeus-Merzbacher studies or their drug apply to Krabbe disease, because the link is only computed and the causing genes differ [e_00a92bfb7837] [e_3dbc42738b5a] [e_1dafbc162208].
